title: BRIN index for time series (PostgreSQL's answer to columnstore-style scans)
claim: Columnstore indexes make analytical scans over millions of rows 10-100x faster with ~10x compression.
PostgreSQL has no columnstore; for append-only time series like metricarchive a BRIN index is the tiny alternative.
verdict: BRIN is the size champion, not the speed champion. On metricarchive.date_c it is 136 kB vs 326 MB for the B-tree
(2,400x smaller) and makes one day {x:day_no_index/day_brin} faster than a full scan. The B-tree is still
faster: {t:day_btree} vs {t:day_brin} for a day, {t:month_btree} vs {t:month_brin} for 30 days. BRIN suits a
rarely queried, append-only archive; keep the B-tree for hot queries. It is not a columnstore: PostgreSQL has no

sections.label: setup
sections.sql:
SET maintenance_work_mem = '1GB';
CREATE INDEX sc_archive_date_brin ON metricarchive USING brin (date_c);

sections.label: Sizes: B-tree vs BRIN on metricarchive.date_c (15M rows)
sections.sql:
SELECT indexrelname AS index, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(indexrelid)) AS size
  FROM pg_stat_user_indexes WHERE indexrelname IN ('metricarchive_date_c', 'sc_archive_date_brin');
